Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Tailwind, Nxeon hosting platform). FIRST STEP: create your own isolated git worktree:
  cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-freemcredesign -b feature/freemc-redesign main
Then `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-freemcredesign`, `ln -s /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules`, `ln -s /opt/nxeon/.env .env`. Do all work there.

CONTEXT: You're redesigning the free Minecraft server dashboard's Overview section. READ FIRST, in full: `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` (the whole file — the top server-info card, the tab strip, and the `Overview` component you're replacing), `app/dashboard/games/page.tsx` (the page that renders it, including the "My Servers / Free Minecraft" tab switcher above it), and `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` for `FREEMC_PRESETS` (note: a parallel agent is simultaneously splitting this into `FREEMC_GAME_TYPES` (9 entries: vanilla/skyblock/prison/towny/parkour/anarchy/lifesteal/missilewars/survivalgames, each with a `heroImage` field) and `FREEMC_GAME_MODES` (4 entries: survival/hardcore/creative/peaceful, simple property sets, no images) plus new server actions `listFreeMinecraftWorlds`/`switchFreeMinecraftGameType`/`applyFreeMinecraftGameMode`/`renameFreeMinecraftWorld`/`deleteFreeMinecraftWorld` in a new `lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts` — build your UI to import and call these exact names once they exist; if the file isn't there yet when you start, write your components assuming that exact contract (documented in detail below) rather than waiting, and note in your report that the wiring needs a final check once both land.

## Exact redesign brief (verbatim from the user, follow precisely)

Redesign the current Nxeon Game Server Overview page. Do not redesign it as a generic dashboard — work directly from the existing layout and preserve its overall Nxeon styling (dark navy/violet, existing `card`/`btn-primary`/`btn-secondary` utility classes, the gradient `from-accent-blue/90 to-brand-500/90` used for active states throughout this codebase).

**Stays unchanged:** the Game Servers page header/hero (`PortalHero`), the "My Servers / Free Minecraft" tab switcher above the server panel, the current server info card for the account's server (name, connect address, IP, status/uptime/CPU/memory stats, Restart/Stop/Console buttons), and the existing Overview/Console/Players/Mods/Roles/Settings/Manage tab strip. Do NOT touch any of that structure or those other tabs' components — only replace what's rendered inside the Overview tab's content.

**One exception to "stays unchanged" — the top server card needs a hero image:** add a large, HD-quality illustrated background image to the right side of that top server-info card (the reference mockup shows a dramatic floating-islands sunset scene with a blocky voxel-style adventurer character holding a sword, warm orange/purple sky). This must be ORIGINAL artwork, not scraped Minecraft/Mojang assets or a literal reproduction of Mojang's "Steve" character design — generate/illustrate an evocative, on-brand equivalent (voxel/blocky-styled generic adventurer silhouette is fine; avoid anything that reads as a direct copy of a specific trademarked character). Match the existing precedent in this codebase: `public/games/art/freemc-skyblock_hero.jpg` etc. were produced by a prior agent as hand-authored SVG→JPEG geometric/gradient art in the Nxeon navy/violet palette (`#0a0e1a`→`#0f1420` background, `#6f47f5`/`#8b5cf6` violet, `#3b82f6`/`#06b6d4` cyan) — you can lean more illustrative/detailed than those (the reference mockup is richer/more scenic), but keep it clearly ORIGINAL and on-brand, not a photoreal Minecraft screenshot pretense.

**Replace the current "Quick-start presets" section entirely with two clearly separated sections:**

1. **"GAME MODE — How you play"** — a compact horizontal row of exactly 4 cards, equal width, for Survival / Hardcore / Creative / Peaceful. Each card: a small icon (grass block for Survival, heart for Hardcore, paint palette for Creative, dove for Peaceful — simple flat/emoji-style icons or small SVGs, not photographic), bold title, one short description line. The currently-selected mode gets a violet glow border (`border-brand-400/50` + a subtle box-shadow glow, plus a small checkmark badge in the corner) — this is a MUCH smaller/lighter visual treatment than the Game Type section below; these are compact utility cards, not hero cards. Clicking selects it and calls `applyFreeMinecraftGameMode` (from the contract above) — this action does NOT restart into a different world, so no "this recreates your server" warning copy is needed here, just "applies instantly" / "restarts to apply" as appropriate (check `lib/game-config.ts`'s existing live-vs-restart field metadata pattern used elsewhere in this dashboard for the phrasing convention).

2. **"GAME TYPE — What you play"** — the main visual focus of the page, MUCH larger than the mode row. A responsive grid (aim for 5 columns on wide screens, wrapping to fewer on narrower ones) of large cinematic cards for Vanilla, SkyBlock, Prison, Towny, Parkour, Lifesteal, Anarchy, Missile Wars, Survival Games (9 total) — each card is dominated by a full-bleed background image (use each type's `heroImage` from `FREEMC_GAME_TYPES` — if a given type doesn't have one yet, fall back gracefully to a plain gradient card, don't break), with a dark gradient scrim at the bottom holding a bold title + short one-line description in white/light text over the image, matching this exact mood per type (reference mockup, describe consistently if you need to touch up/regenerate any missing hero images): Vanilla = a calm sunset landscape with a small house/tree silhouette; SkyBlock = floating island with a tree; Prison = a dim prison corridor with cell bars and a cold blue glow; Towny = a hillside fantasy town at dusk with warm lantern-lit windows; Parkour = a character mid-leap over floating checkered platforms at golden-hour; Lifesteal = a glowing pixel/voxel heart on near-black; Anarchy = a "TNT" block with fire/explosion energy, red/orange danger tones; Missile Wars = missiles launching into a fiery sky; Survival Games = two silhouetted characters squaring off with weapons in a forest clearing. The selected type gets a strong violet glow border + checkmark badge (bigger/more prominent than the mode row's, since this is the primary visual selector on the page). Clicking a card selects it, and a confirm/apply action calls `switchFreeMinecraftGameType` (from the contract) — THIS one DOES need clear "applying this switches your world and restarts your server" warning copy, since it's a heavier operation (matches the current codebase's existing copy tone: "Applying a preset restarts your server. Presets that add plugins take a little longer the first time while they download.").

**Explicitly do NOT add:** a Quick Actions panel, a Server Info side panel, or a Resource Usage side panel — the existing top server card already covers server info/controls, don't duplicate it.

**Also build a "Saved Worlds" view** (the user asked, separately, for "an option to see all of the saved worlds in the dashboard and be able to edit them") — add this as a section within the redesigned Overview tab (a collapsible/expandable panel below the Game Type grid, or a small "View saved worlds" toggle/link that reveals a list — your call on the exact placement, keep it uncluttered) showing every world from `listFreeMinecraftWorlds()`: game type label, when last played, a "Switch to this world" action (calls `switchFreeMinecraftGameType`), a rename control (calls `renameFreeMinecraftWorld`), and a delete control (calls `deleteFreeMinecraftWorld`, with a confirmation step — this is destructive). The currently-active world should be visually marked and its delete control disabled (matches the contract's own refusal rule).

## Build
- Rewrite the `Overview` component in `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` — actually, to avoid conflicting with the worlds-backend agent who may also be touching that file's imports, build this as NEW self-contained components instead: `components/customer/freemc/GameModeSelector.tsx`, `components/customer/freemc/GameTypeGrid.tsx`, `components/customer/freemc/SavedWorldsPanel.tsx`, and a `components/customer/freemc/OverviewRedesigned.tsx` that composes all three plus a hero-image prop for the top card. Do NOT edit `FreeMcDashboard.tsx` itself — I'll do the final wiring (swapping the old `Overview` for `OverviewRedesigned` and adding the hero image to the top card) once both your work and the backend agent's land, since editing that shared file from two parallel agents risks an unmergeable conflict.
- Produce/regenerate hero images as needed: reuse existing `public/games/art/freemc-<type>_hero.jpg` files where they already exist and look right (check what's there); only generate NEW art for the top-card hero image and for any game type currently missing one or whose existing image doesn't read as "large card, cinematic, dominant" at bigger display size (the existing ones were sized/composed for a small thumbnail strip — check `public/games/art/freemc-*.jpg` and judge whether they hold up enlarged; regenerate if they look thin/sparse at card-hero scale).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and a full `npm run build` must both pass clean.
- Commit explicitly named files (never `-A`). Don't merge to main, don't delete your worktree.

Report back: file paths created, which hero images you reused vs regenerated and why, how you handled the "backend contract not built yet" risk if it applied, and confirmation build/typecheck passed.

1	/**
2	 * Docker/RCON control primitives for free-tier Minecraft containers on
3	 * freemc-host — the free-tier equivalent of lib/game-control.ts, which speaks
4	 * to full Proxmox-VM game servers over SSH+tunnelled RCON. This is much
5	 * simpler: one SSH hop to the host, then `docker exec <container> ...` for
6	 * everything, using the CLI tools itzg/docker-minecraft-server already bundles
7	 * (rcon-cli, mc-monitor) instead of a hand-rolled RCON protocol client.
8	 *
9	 * Plain module (no "use server") — imported from both lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts
10	 * and, in future, a worker sweep, same reasoning as lib/game-control.ts.
11	 */
12	import { scryptSync } from "node:crypto";
13	import type { Client } from "ssh2";
14	import { exec, execInput, shellQuote } from "./ssh-exec";
15	
16	/**
17	 * Deterministic per-server RCON password — HMAC-shaped via scrypt off
18	 * AUTH_SECRET, same derivation pattern as lib/crypto-box.ts's BYOK key (just a
19	 * different domain-separation salt). Never stored: computed identically at
20	 * container-creation time and every time we need to talk RCON to it, so a
21	 * restart/recreate never invalidates it and there's nothing to leak from the DB.
22	 */
23	export function rconPasswordFor(ownerId: string): string {
24	  const secret = process.env.AUTH_SECRET;
25	  if (!secret || !secret.trim()) throw new Error("AUTH_SECRET is not set — cannot derive RCON password");
26	  return scryptSync(secret, `nxeon-freemc-rcon:${ownerId}`, 24).toString("base64url");
27	}
28	
29	/** Run one command inside a container via `docker exec`. */
30	async function dockerExec(conn: Client, containerName: string, cmd: string, timeoutMs = 15_000) {
31	  return exec(conn, `docker exec ${shellQuote(containerName)} ${cmd}`, timeoutMs);
32	}
33	
34	export type ServerStatus = {
35	  running: boolean;
36	  players: { online: number; max: number } | null;
37	};
38	
39	/**
40	 * Best-effort status via mc-monitor (bundled in the image) — a plain status
41	 * ping, no RCON auth needed. A stopped/sleeping container (mc-router scaled it
42	 * to zero) just fails the docker exec, which reads as "not running", not an
43	 * error — that's the expected, common state for a free server nobody's on.
44	 */
45	export async function getFreeServerStatus(conn: Client, containerName: string): Promise<ServerStatus> {
46	  const inspect = await exec(
47	    conn,
48	    `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`,
49	    10_000,
50	  );
51	  if (inspect.code !== 0 || inspect.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
52	    return { running: false, players: null };
53	  }
54	  const status = await dockerExec(
55	    conn,
56	    containerName,
57	    "mc-monitor status --host localhost --port 25565 --json",
58	    10_000,
59	  );
60	  if (status.code !== 0) return { running: true, players: null }; // container up, MC still booting
61	  try {
62	    const parsed = JSON.parse(status.stdout);
63	    const p = parsed?.server_info?.players;
64	    if (typeof p?.online === "number" && typeof p?.max === "number") {
65	      return { running: true, players: { online: p.online, max: p.max } };
66	    }
67	  } catch {
68	    /* fall through */
69	  }
70	  return { running: true, players: null };
71	}
72	
73	export type RconResult = { ok: true; response: string } | { ok: false; error: string };
74	
75	/** One RCON round-trip via the bundled rcon-cli — see lib/game-control.ts's
76	 *  validateRconCommand for the same input sanitation used on the paid path. */
77	export async function sendRcon(
78	  conn: Client,
79	  containerName: string,
80	  ownerId: string,
81	  command: string,
82	): Promise<RconResult> {
83	  const password = rconPasswordFor(ownerId);
84	  const r = await dockerExec(
85	    conn,
86	    containerName,
87	    `env RCON_PASSWORD=${shellQuote(password)} rcon-cli ${shellQuote(command)}`,
88	    12_000,
89	  );
90	  if (r.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: r.stderr.trim() || "RCON command failed." };
91	  return { ok: true, response: r.stdout.trim() };
92	}
93	
94	export type PlayerInfo = { name: string };
95	
96	/** Parses rcon-cli's `list` response: "There are N of a max of M players online: a, b, c" */
97	export async function getFreeServerPlayers(
98	  conn: Client,
99	  containerName: string,
100	  ownerId: string,
101	): Promise<{ ok: true; players: PlayerInfo[] } | { ok: false; error: string }> {
102	  const r = await sendRcon(conn, containerName, ownerId, "list");
103	  if (!r.ok) return r;
104	  const colonIdx = r.response.indexOf(":");
105	  if (colonIdx === -1) return { ok: true, players: [] };
106	  const names = r.response
107	    .slice(colonIdx + 1)
108	    .split(",")
109	    .map((s) => s.trim())
110	    .filter(Boolean);
111	  return { ok: true, players: names.map((name) => ({ name })) };
112	}
113	
114	/** Reads /data/server.properties into a plain key->value map. */
115	export async function readServerProperties(
116	  conn: Client,
117	  containerName: string,
118	): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
119	  const r = await dockerExec(conn, containerName, "cat /data/server.properties", 10_000);
120	  if (r.code !== 0) return {};
121	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
122	  for (const line of r.stdout.split("\n")) {
123	    if (!line || line.startsWith("#")) continue;
124	    const i = line.indexOf("=");
125	    if (i === -1) continue;
126	    out[line.slice(0, i).trim()] = line.slice(i + 1).trim();
127	  }
128	  return out;
129	}

131	/**
132	 * Writes a set of server.properties keys in place (sed-style line replace,
133	 * appending any key not already present) and restarts the container so the
134	 * itzg entrypoint's normal boot sequence picks the new values up — the image
135	 * only reads server.properties at startup (confirmed against the Minecraft
136	 * wiki: none of gamemode/motd/max-players/etc. persist a live RCON change back
137	 * to the file), so a restart is the only fully-reliable way to apply anything
138	 * here. Keys with a real live RCON equivalent (difficulty, whitelist on/off)
139	 * are ALSO pushed live by the caller for instant effect — see FIELD_LIVE_CMD.
140	 */
141	export async function writeServerProperties(
142	  conn: Client,
143	  containerName: string,
144	  changes: Record<string, string>,
145	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
146	  const current = await readServerProperties(conn, containerName);
147	  const merged = { ...current, ...changes };
148	  const body = Object.entries(merged)
149	    .map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`)
150	    .join("\n");
151	  const write = await execInput(
152	    conn,
153	    `docker exec -i ${shellQuote(containerName)} sh -c 'cat > /data/server.properties'`,
154	    body + "\n",
155	    10_000,
156	  );
157	  if (write.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: write.stderr.trim() || "Could not write server.properties." };

167	 *  value. MOTD and max-players have no vanilla live command at all. */
168	export function liveRconCommandFor(key: string, value: string): string | null {
